He kept the genocide characterization after apologizing in Sept 2026 for remarks about Jewish Mainers. This matches or exceeds Sanders (opposes all military aid, not just offensive arms).
evidence_1: "the Israeli government is committing genocide in Gaza" (X post, via Common Dreams)
evidence_2: "I'll never vote in favor of US taxpayer-funded military aid to Israel"
evidence_3: "I believe what's happening in Gaza is genocide"
evidence_4: "I don't want the United States sending money, a blank check, to him" (Netanyahu)

JTA and KTTC report she has called the war a genocide (Tafoya attacked her for it in the debate; no disavowal reported). She keeps two-state language and has not opposed defensive aid like Iron Dome, which is in line with Sanders rather than beyond.

rationale: Markey voted Yea on all 9 Sanders resolutions to block offensive arms sales to Israel (2024-25) and campaigned in 2026 on being among the first to oppose bomb sales. He condemns the war sharply (an 'unconscionable war against Gaza', indiscriminate bombing, tens of thousands of innocent Palestinian dead). But he frames it as a Netanyahu-government problem, reaffirms Israel's right to defend itself, and I found no genocide or ethnic-cleansing characterization, so he stops short of level 4.
evidence_1: Netanyahu's "unbelievably unconscionable war against Gaza" (MA Senate debate)
evidence_2: "the loss of tens of thousands of innocent Palestinian lives" (arms-resolution statement)
evidence_3: Stop giving Netanyahu's government "a blank check for offensive weapons"
evidence_4: Senate votes: Yea on 9 of 9 Sanders joint resolutions of disapproval (2024-2025)
notes: markey.senate.gov returns 403 to fetcher; release text read via capitolreleases mirror and news. April 2025 statement reaffirms Israel's right to defend itself. No genocide language found in searches. Vote tally from task brief.

evidence_1: Israel commits "human rights abuses, genocide and apartheid" (Senate primary debate)

rationale: Nixon said after winning the primary that she opposes sending any money or weapons to Israel right now and called Netanyahu a war criminal who must answer for his crimes. In 2023, as a Florida legislator, she introduced a Gaza ceasefire resolution and called it a massacre that had wiped out entire Palestinian bloodlines. Cutting off all aid and calling the conduct an atrocity together go as far as or beyond Sanders.
evidence_1: "I do not support sending any money or any weapons to Israel at this moment" (MS NOW)
evidence_2: Netanyahu "is a war criminal who needs to answer to his crimes"
evidence_3: "Entire bloodlines of Palestinians have been wiped away" (FL House floor)
evidence_4: "A massacre is occurring now" (FL House floor, ceasefire resolution)
notes: Ynet and other outlets say she calls it genocide; I did not verify that word in her own speech, but the substance (no weapons, war criminal, massacre) is level 4 either way. The 2023 floor quotes are via Mondoweiss, which embeds the video; a WLRN 2023-11-08 piece covers the resolution debate.

rationale: Pappas calls himself a strong supporter of the US-Israel relationship, took AIPAC PAC money, and declined to back the July 2026 Massie amendment cutting aid to Israel (voted present, calling it overly broad). But in 2025-26 he explicitly criticized the 'disproportionate, extreme policies' of Netanyahu's government, called for a 'reset' in the relationship and for Netanyahu to go, and said he was horrified by famine in Gaza. Clear criticism of the government's conduct with no arms limits puts him at 2, at the low end.
evidence_1: Opposes "the disproportionate, extreme policies of the Netanyahu government" (Massie amendment statement)
evidence_2: "This is a moment for a reset in that relationship." Hopes Netanyahu is "on his way out"
evidence_3: "I am horrified by reports of famine and widespread starvation in Gaza."
evidence_4: "I'm a strong supporter of the bipartisan U.S.-Israel relationship" (AIPAC summit video)
notes: Borderline 1/2: he backs aid and took AIPAC PAC money (per brief), but his campaign-period criticism of Netanyahu's conduct is specific, not generic. He voted present, not no, on the Massie amendment.

rationale: In Feb 2026 Osborn accepted A New Policy PAC's endorsement and said US tax dollars pay for bombs that knock over hospitals and that 'Made in the USA' should not be on bombs that kill kids. That is pointed criticism of US-armed Israeli conduct, and he ran an ad attacking Ricketts's AIPAC backing. But I found no explicit commitment from him to block or condition arms or aid, and in 2024 his spokesperson called Israel's response justified. So 2: clearly critical, no stated arms limit.
evidence_1: Tax dollars "pay for bombs that knock over hospitals in other countries"
evidence_2: "Made in the USA" should not be shameful "when it's written on bombs that kill kids"
evidence_3: Campaign-shared ad: Ricketts sides with "AIPAC and defense contractors"
evidence_4: Spokesperson (2024): Osborn "thinks Israel's response [to Oct. 7] was justified" (via JI, citing American Prospect)
notes: Thin record. His 2026 rhetoric implies opposition to the bombs, but he never explicitly calls for blocking arms. The endorsing group favors cutting or conditioning aid, but the rubric treats group positions as leads, not his position. Could be 3 if a firmer arms statement turns up. Gaza is not named in the quotes I found, though the context (ANP endorsement) is Israel.

rationale: Brown is a self-described pro-Israel progressive. He voted Nay on all 3 Sanders arms-resolution votes in 2024, voted for military aid, and once sponsored a long-term Israel security assistance authorization. His stated position stresses Israel's right to defend itself, plus humanitarian aid to Gaza and a ceasefire-for-hostages deal. I found no 2025-26 campaign statement criticizing Netanyahu or the conduct of the war, which is mainstream support with concern.
evidence_1: Spokesperson: "Israel has a clear and undeniable right to defend itself"
evidence_2: Spokesperson: Israel and Hamas "must agree to a ceasefire that ends the war, frees the hostages"
evidence_3: Voted Nay on 3 of 3 Sanders joint resolutions blocking arms sales (Nov 2024)
notes: No direct 2025-26 campaign quotes found; his campaign didn't respond to JTA (2026-11-02). J Street supporters bundled $800k+ for him (JTA). Rating rests mainly on 2024 record, which is older than the campaign period.

rationale: Peltola's only substantive record is from her time in the House. In May 2024 she was one of 16 Democrats who voted to stop the Biden administration from withholding military aid to Israel, which means opposing the one condition then in play. She also voted for the Feb 2024 stand-alone Israel aid package and for ICC sanctions. Her 2026 campaign declined repeated requests to say whether she still holds these positions, and I found no statement of concern for Gaza civilians. On the record available, this is unconditional support.
evidence_1: Voted with Republicans to stop Biden "withholding military aid to Israel" (one of 16 Democrats)
evidence_2: Voted for Feb 2024 stand-alone Israel aid package; backed ICC sanctions (JI report of votes)
evidence_3: 2026 campaign "did not respond" to repeated questions on whether her stance changed (JI)
notes: Rests on votes only; I found no statements by her on Israel/Gaza. Could be 1 if a statement of civilian concern exists (none found). Ketchikan Daily News lead returned HTTP 429 and was not retried. She is silent in the 2026 campaign, so this reflects her last known record.

rationale: Turek calls Israel an ally but says there are limits to what the US should do, and called the response 'disproportionate' (Gazette, context and date not fully verified). In the Iowa House he backed a failed amendment conditioning support for Israel on adherence to international humanitarian law, then voted for the final pro-Israel resolution. His campaign declined to take a position on suspending arms sales. Mild but real criticism of the conduct, no commitment on arms: a soft 2.

evidence_2: Backed Iowa House amendment conditioning support on Israel's "adherence to international humanitarian law" (JI; amendment text)
evidence_3: Campaign "declined to comment" on suspending US arms sales to Israel (JI)

If that quote is about something else, he drops to 1 (voted for the final pro-Israel resolution). No Israel exchange found in the Senate debates.

rationale: Ossoff voted Yea on 5 of 9 Sanders resolutions to block arms sales. In July 2025 he voted to block rifles likely bound for Ben-Gvir's police, citing the starvation of Gaza's children, but voted against blocking the bomb package. In the Oct 2026 debate he stood by those votes, said Israeli forces 'violated the law of armed conflict' in Gaza, and defended ICC accountability for crimes against humanity. He declined to call it genocide (leaving that to the ICC) and still affirms support for Israelis' security. Selective arms limits plus a war-crimes-level condemnation is 3, at the lower edge.

evidence_2: Genocide is "a question for the International Criminal Court" (debate)
evidence_3: Cites "the intolerable starvation of children"; opposes Netanyahu's conduct of the war (arms vote statement)
evidence_4: Senate votes: Yea on 5 of 9 Sanders joint resolutions; split in July 2025 (rifles yes, bombs no)

Vote tally from task brief.

rationale: Hamilton told Politico in Oct 2026 that he doesn't want his tax money paying for weapons dropped on hospitals and destroying communities. That means stopping offensive weapons, though when pressed he said 'not all weapons transfers'. He called the war 'irresponsible and unjust' and said the actions 'feel genocidal', while declining the genocide label because he doesn't see intent. He affirms Israel's right to security and that Hamas must go. Restricting offensive arms with sharp condemnation, short of the genocide charge, is level 3.

evidence_2: Called Israel's war in Gaza "irresponsible and unjust"
evidence_3: "I wouldn't use the word 'genocide'" but "these actions feel genocidal"
evidence_4: "I want them to stop dropping bombs on innocent people."
notes: Single interview (Politico video via Jewish Insider). 'Not all weapons transfers' implies offensive-only limits, consistent with Sanders's resolutions but not a full cutoff. Did not search the original Politico video further.

He never directly criticizes Netanyahu or the conduct of the war beyond the aid point, so this is mainstream support with concern, at the upper edge of 1.

rationale: Talarico said in Aug 2026 he would not vote to send weapons to the Netanyahu government, and that aid should be conditioned on ending the death and destruction in Gaza and the West Bank. At the Oct 2026 CNN town hall he condemned Netanyahu for waging war on civilians and using collective punishment. He declines the genocide label, deferring to the ICJ while saying there is evidence for the charge, and affirms Israel's right to defend itself. That is a strong level 3, short of 4 only on the genocide characterization.
